questions.stem:
An ac voltage \(V_i = 12 \sin (100 \pi t)\)V is applied between points A and B in a network of two ideal diodes and three resistors as shown in figure.
During the positive half-cycle of the input voltage \(V_i\) supplied to the network.
(a) Identify which of the two diodes will conduct and why ?
(b) Redraw an equivalent circuit diagram to show the flow of current.
(c) Calculate the output voltage drops \(V_0\) across the three resistors when the input voltage attains its peak value.
questions._figure: REQUIRED — the stem says 'as shown in figure' and names no connection; part (a) asks which diode conducts, which is decided entirely by how the two diodes are drawn. DESCRIBED: a diamond-shaped network whose four corners are labelled A (top), P (left), R (right) and B (bottom); a diode labelled \(D_1\) sits in the upper-left arm between P and A, a diode labelled \(D_2\) in the upper-right arm between A and R; a 1 k\(\Omega\) resistor is drawn horizontally across the middle between P and R; a 2 k\(\Omega\) resistor sits in the lower-left arm between P and B and a 3 k\(\Omega\) resistor in the lower-right arm between R and B; an ac source marked \(V_i\) is connected on the left through an outer rectangular loop that joins the top and bottom corners. DELIBERATELY WITHHELD: the ORIENTATION of each diode symbol, i.e. which way its triangle and bar point — that is exactly the discrimination part (a) tests. Page idx 14.
questions._flag: AMBIGUOUS AS PRINTED, and CBSE's own marking scheme accepts BOTH readings — not a void (no 'award full mark regardless' wording), but a real finding. The stem says 'During the positive half-cycle' without stating which of A and B is then positive, so the scheme prints a primary answer (\(D_2\) conducts; \(V_{RP}\) = 4 V, \(V_{PB}\) = 8 V, \(V_{RB}\) = 12 V) AND an 'Alternatively: If the student considers positive AC cycle reaching diode \(D_1\)' branch with a different set of drops (\(V_{PB}\) = 12 V, \(V_{PR}\) = 3 V, \(V_{RB}\) = 9 V). Flagged so a single model answer is not authored later as though only one reading existed.

questions.stem:
Figure shows a narrow beam of electrons entering with a velocity of \(3 \times 10^7\) m/s, symmetrically through the space between two parallel horizontal plates \(P_1 P_1'\) and \(P_2 P_2'\) kept 2 cm apart.
If each plate is 3 cm long, calculate the potential difference V applied between the plates so that the beam just strikes the end \(P_2'\).
questions._figure: REQUIRED — the stem opens 'Figure shows ...' and names the plate labels only through it, so a missing drawing leaves a dangling reference. DESCRIBED: two long horizontal plates drawn one above the other, the upper labelled \(P_1\) at its left end and \(P_1'\) at its right, the lower labelled \(P_2\) and \(P_2'\); a source marked V is connected between them; an electron marked '-e, m' enters horizontally from the left, midway between the plates, and a dashed line traces its path, running straight at first and then curving until an arrowhead meets the right-hand edge of the lower plate. Nothing is withheld: the drawing carries no quantity the stem does not already state (plate separation 2 cm, plate length 3 cm, entry 'symmetrically', beam 'just strikes the end \(P_2'\)'), so it is arguably illustrative — marked REQUIRED because the stem cites it by name and the guidance is to choose REQUIRED when unsure. Page idx 14.

(b) A transparent container contains layers of three immiscible transparent liquids A, B and C of refractive indices n, \(\frac{3}{4} n\) and \(\frac{2}{3} n\), respectively. A laser beam is incident at the interface between A and B at an angle \(\theta\) as shown in figure. Prove that the beam does not enter region C at all for \(\sin \theta \ge \frac{2}{3}\).
questions._figure: REQUIRED — part (b) says 'as shown in figure', and the STACKING ORDER of the three liquids and the reference line from which \(\theta\) is measured exist only in the drawing. DESCRIBED: a rectangular container seen in cross-section, divided by two horizontal interfaces into three stippled layers; the lowest is labelled A on its right and n on its left, the middle is labelled B and \(\frac{3}{4} n\), the topmost is labelled C and \(\frac{2}{3} n\); a straight ray enters from the lower left, meets the A-B interface, and the angle \(\theta\) is marked there between the ray and a short vertical normal drawn at the point of incidence. Nothing is withheld — the question is a derivation, not a discrimination between drawn alternatives, so a full reading of the layout gives none of it away. Page idx 16.

(b) Find net resistance of the network of resistors connected between A and B, as shown in figure.
questions._figure: REQUIRED — part (b) says 'as shown in figure' and the stem names no resistor and no connection; the whole network exists only in the drawing. DESCRIBED: a resistor ladder drawn between two end terminals labelled A (far left) and B (far right), with four further labelled junctions M, O, P and N along it, and six resistors carrying the printed labels 2R, R, R, R, R and 3R. DELIBERATELY WITHHELD: which resistor spans which pair of junctions, and which two form the bridge arms above and below — that topology IS the question, because the whole calculation turns on recognising a balanced Wheatstone bridge between M and N. questions.context: A galvanometer is used to detect or/and measure small currents in an electrical circuit. It essentially works on the fact that a current-carrying coil experiences a deflecting torque when placed in a magnetic field. This deflection in the coil can be measured and it is related to the current flowing in the coil, the number of turns in the coil, area of the coil and the magnetic field. A hair spring attached to the coil provides a counter torque and helps in measuring the deflection. A galvanometer can be converted to an ammeter or a voltmeter of desired range by using suitable resistances.

questions.subtopic: Refraction at Spherical Surfaces and by Lenses
questions.stem:
(a) Using the relation for refraction at a curved spherical surface, derive the expression for lens maker's formula.
(b) Three lenses \(L_1\), \(L_2\) and \(L_3\), each of focal length 40 cm, are placed coaxially. The distance between \(L_1\) and \(L_2\) and between \(L_2\) and \(L_3\) are 120 cm and 20 cm respectively. An object is kept at a distance of 80 cm to the left of lens \(L_1\).
Find the distance of the final image formed from the object.

(a) Draw a ray diagram to show the image formation by a concave mirror when the object is kept between its focus and the centre of curvature. Using this diagram, derive the mirror formula.
(b) A concave mirror produces a two times magnified virtual image of an object kept 10 cm in front of it. Calculate the focal length of the mirror.

(a) State Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction.
(b) Derive an expression for the self-inductance of an air-filled long solenoid of length \(l\) and cross-sectional area A having N turns.
(c) A conducting rod of length 50 cm, with one end pivoted, is rotated with angular speed of 60 rpm in a uniform magnetic field of 4.0 mT directed perpendicular to the plane of rotation of rod. Find the emf induced in the rod.

(a) Draw a labelled diagram of a step-up transformer. State the principle on which it works and obtain the ratio of secondary voltage to primary voltage in terms of number of turns and currents in the two coils.
(b) The ratio of the number of turns in the primary to the secondary of an ideal transformer is 1 : 5. If 5 kW power at 200 V is supplied to the primary, find
(i) current in the primary, and
(ii) output voltage.

questions.subtopic: Electric Dipole and Dipole in a Uniform Field
questions.stem:
(a) An electric dipole consists of two point charges q and -q separated by a distance 2a. Derive an expression for the electric field \(\vec{E}\) due to this dipole at a point distant r from the centre of the dipole on the equatorial plane. Write the expression for the electric field at a far off point, i.e. r >> a.
(b) A dipole is placed in x-y plane such that charges q and -q are located at \(x = a\) and \(x = b\) respectively. There exists an electric field \(\vec{E} = 2 \hat{i}\ \frac{\mathrm{N}}{\mathrm{C}}\) in the region. Calculate the force \(\vec{F}\) and torque \(\vec{\tau}\) experienced by the dipole.

(a) Two cells of emf \(E_1\) and \(E_2\) with internal resistances \(r_1\) and \(r_2\) respectively, are connected in parallel by connecting their positive terminals together and negative terminals together. Deduce an expression for equivalent emf and equivalent internal resistance of the combination.
(b) A parallel combination, as stated in (a) above, of two cells of emfs E and 3E and internal resistances R each is connected across a resistance 2R. Find the current that flows through resistance 2R.
